title: Conversational traceback failure retro
summary: On 2026-09-30 we observed a high-severity degradation of the Hosted API manifested as a sharp rise in streaming fragment drops and elevated 5xx rates across multiple regions. The incident lasted ~28 minutes and primarily affected conversational streaming endpoints (chat/stream). Root cause was a cascading failure in the conversational traceback path: an interaction between a recent KV-cache eviction change, an edge-proxy backpressure harmonic, and a scheduler coalescing regression. This produced large prefix-miss churn and excessive inter-node hedging which saturated acceptor queues and surfaced as increased TTFB and 5xx responses.
impact: Start: 2026-09-30T09:12:00Z, End: 2026-09-30T09:40:00Z. ~28 minutes of elevated errors/p99 latency. Affected customers: ~120 (high-traffic tenants), global error rate peaked at 4.8% (baseline ~0.15%). Streaming fragment drop rate increased 35x for chat streams. Consumer-visible failures: partial streams (silence after initial tokens) and spiky 500/503 responses. No data loss; no security impact. Estimated revenue impact: transient throttled traffic; estimated <0.1% monthly revenue delta but significant customer support load.
detection: Automated SLO alerts for streaming p95/p99 latency and 5xx rate fired first (09:14 UTC). On-call SRE paged by alerting Slack at 09:15. Customer support tickets and CSE Slack threads corroborated the scope by 09:18. Synthetic streaming probes showed fragment reassembly failures by 09:13; those traces were the earliest signal but were not routed to the primary on-call until aggregated with error-rate alerts.
timeline:
09:12:20Z - Synthetic probe spike observed (fragment reassembly errors)
09:13:05Z - Streaming p99 and 5xx SLO alerts begin to fire (edge and acceptor layers)
09:14:00Z - On-call SRE (Aisha) paged and begins triage; initial hypothesis: edge TLS flakiness
09:16:30Z - Traces show correlated KV-cache eviction storms on backend shards; observed high prefix-miss rates
09:18:15Z - Evidence of hedging amplification: hedged requests multiplied across acceptor pool causing queue buildup
09:20:40Z - Mitigation 1: Disabled hedging policy for affected tenant shard groups (quick rollback) — immediate improvement in queue depth but errors persisted for some streams
09:22:00Z - Mitigation 2: Applied emergency backpressure cap at edge-proxy for streaming paths; p95 improved, p99 still elevated
09:30:00Z - Root cause tracing identifies a recent KV eviction parameter change (merge commit in PR 2817) that increased eviction aggressiveness during bursty workloads
09:33:45Z - Rollback of KV-cache eviction param to previous safe value enacted; streaming fragment drops drop to baseline within ~5 minutes
09:40:00Z - All alerts return to normal; incident declared resolved at 09:42 UTC after monitoring window
root_cause: Three-layer interaction under burst load: 1) A recently merged change (serving-runtime PR 2817) adjusted KV-cache eviction thresholds to reduce memory usage but made eviction decisions less burst-stable. 2) Under prefix-skewed conversational workloads, this produced rapid prefix-miss churn and heavy rehydration traffic. 3) The acceptor and edge hedging logic reacted to transient latency by spawning hedged requests; the hedging multiplier and scheduler coalescing regression caused amplified concurrent requests against the same backend shards, saturating acceptor queues and causing TCP backpressure and 5xx errors. The incident is therefore a systemic emergent property, not a single line-of-code bug.
mitigation: Short term: disabled hedging for affected streaming routes; applied emergency backpressure cap at edge-proxy; rolled back KV-cache eviction param to prior configuration. Medium term: revert and patch the serving-runtime change to make eviction behavior burst-resilient and add safety gating (see followups). Long term: introduce a regression test harness that simulates prefix-skewed conversational workloads to catch eviction/rehydration cascades; harden hedging and scheduler coalescing to respect per-shard concurrency windows.
rollback: Immediate rollback of the eviction aggressiveness change (config revert) applied at 09:33:45Z. The PR was reverted and a follow-up patch prepared to introduce a graceful eviction ramp and telemetry gates before reintroducing the optimization.
followups:
1) Serve-time test harness: create replayable traffic fixture that reproduces prefix-skewed conversation bursts (owner: Marco, due 2026-10-12).
2) Hedging policy revision: cap hedging multiplier and add sliding window guard (owner: Jenna, due 2026-10-08).
3) Scheduler coalescing audit: add unit tests and runtime circuit-breaker to avoid coalescer regression impact (owner: Omar, due 2026-10-15).
4) KV-cache telemetry: emit eviction storm alerts and per-shard rehydration QPS (owner: Priya, due 2026-10-06).
5) Runbook update: add troubleshooting checklist for streaming fragment-drop incidents and rapid rollback playbook (owner: eng-sre, due 2026-10-04).
action_items: Add a synthetic probe specifically for conversational fragment reassembly and route its alerts to the streaming on-call rotation (owner: Marco, due 2026-10-04)
Introduce a canary gating step in CI for KV-cache eviction changes that runs the bursty convo fixture (owner: Priya, due 2026-10-12)
Limit hedging multiplier to 1.5x and add a per-shard inflight cap in the acceptor (owner: Jenna, due 2026-10-08)
Create dashboard tile that correlates prefix-miss rate, rehydration QPS, acceptor queue depth, and 5xx rate (owner: Omar, due 2026-10-06)
Post-incident customer outreach: draft status update and RCA for affected tenants (owner: Aisha, due 2026-10-02)
Add a short FAQ for support on how hedging and eviction interact and recommended config knobs for Dedicated customers (owner: Solutions Eng, due 2026-10-14)
notes_to_self: We leaned too quickly on hedging rollback as the entire solution; the real win was the eviction param revert. Next time, triage should prioritize cache telemetry and rehydration signals earlier in the hypothesis tree. Also: ensure that synthetic conversational probes escalate to SRE channel separate from generic CMs so signals are not lost in alert noise.
postmortem_contributors: Aisha Patel, Marco Ruiz, Jenna Liu, Omar Haddad, Priya Menon
